newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday July 28.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi said this would be the last summer Italians would have to make sacrifices to help Italy join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). Prodi meets centre-left government's allies on Tuesday in talks on welfare state reforms (all).
* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said his party did not back any further cuts to welfare state spending and was not ready to endure any more sacrifices (all).

* In an interview, trade unions' leader Sergio Cofferati said autumn would be hard in terms of economic sacrifices but welfare state reforms talks would proceed and benefit from political stability. Cofferati repeated the government's main target should be to boost employment (La Repubblica).

* Italian Treasury warned ministries should control spending in late 1997 to ensure Italy qualifies for EMU in 1999. According to the ministry, public education, public employment, posts, transport, health and defence sectors are all at risk of overspending but the main problem is pensions' spending (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
